text:
arjun: Heads-up — overnight (02:00-03:30 UTC) deploybot auto-pinned several runtime/model combos in eu-west after latency spikes. Not sure if this is expected behavior or a config flake. Anyone on-call?

deploybot: INFO pinned runtime:3.1 -> runtime:3.0 on pool:hosted-eu-west at 2026-03-19T02:12:03Z (trigger: p90 latency > 250ms for 60s). See /deploys/604860-eviction-log

maya: I saw this on perf dashboard — p90 for llama3q-16k jumped around 270-350ms for a bit. Root increase coincides with yesterday's kernel-selector release (kernel-sel v7) that landed in canary.

ellie: +1, I traced a few traces to KV cache churn;  some requests hit fallback kernels which are slower. Not all regions affected; eu-west seems worst.

samir: Was there a pinned-versions guard for runtime/model combos? I thought deploybot only pins when degradation sustained for >5m. Deploybot message shows 60s — is that new?

arjun: Good point. I think ops-config short-circuit was added in the aggressive-safety experiment. @maya can you confirm if we flipped that flag?

maya: Confirmed — ops/experiments/aggressive-safety was enabled for nightshift to auto-protect SLOs. It uses 60s window. We rolled it to 300s in staging but forgot to propagate the change to eu-west. My bad.

ellie: Ok that's the cause. We should either revert the aggressive flag or do a targeted rollback of kernel-sel v7 in eu-west. Which is less disruptive?

samir: Targeted rollback of kernel-sel in eu-west is lower blast radius — leaves global rollout intact. But note: rollback path requires coordination with infra to avoid thrash on warming.

arjun: Proposal: schedule a targeted rollback of kernel-sel v7 on eu-west at 03:50 UTC (in 20m), pause aggressive-safety, and let pinned runtime fall back naturally. Also publish a short release note and an internal postmortem stub. Any objections?

maya: No objections. I'll patch ops/experiments to set aggressive-safety -> 300s for eu-west now, and prepare rollback job.

deploybot: SCHEDULED rollback job: rollback-kernel-sel-v7 -> eu-west at 2026-03-19T03:50:00Z (initiated by maya). Job id: rb-604860-01

ellie: After rollback, we should run the KV stress harness against a canary subset for 30m to ensure cache behavior stabilizes. If p90 remains <240ms and error rate normal, we can unpin runtime on pinned hosts.

arjun: Agree. Also prepare release-note entry for public changelog: short, factual. Internal release note (for infra/product) should include timeline + rollback rationale. Sample snippet:

```
Release note (internal): 2026-03-19: Rolled back kernel-selector v7 in eu-west due to observed p90 latency regressions on llama3q-16k. Rollback executed to restore latency SLOs; aggressive auto-pinning experiment inadvertently shortened the detection window. Follow-up: sync staging flag propagation and add a 5m cooldown to auto-pinning.
```

samir: I'll add an item to the runbook: "If aggressive-safety enabled, verify experiment flag sync across regions before night windows" and link to incident tracking.

maya: rollback started (rb-604860-01) — deploybot logs show phased revert across 6 hosts. I'll monitor.

deploybot: INFO rollback phase1 complete (3/6 hosts) at 2026-03-19T03:56:12Z

ellie: p90 on the warmup workers already dropping to ~230ms. Good sign.

deploybot: INFO rollback complete (6/6 hosts) at 2026-03-19T04:07:21Z

maya: Aggressive-safety flag set back to 300s in eu-west. I also disabled auto-notify for ephemeral pins to reduce noise.

arjun: Great. Action items: 1) maya to follow up with PR to sync experiment configs across regions, 2) ellie to run 30m KV stress and post telemetry snippet, 3) samir to update runbook and add cooldown guidance, 4) ops to add a canary check before auto-pin threshold reduction.

samir: Noted and will own runbook/update.

ellie: KV stress done 30m — p90 stable at 228ms, no elevated errors. Posting charts to /observability/threads/604860 for follow-up.

deploybot: INFO unpin queued for hosts that were auto-pinned (reason: manual rollback restored kernel performance). Unpin scheduled at 2026-03-19T04:30:00Z

arjun: Cool. Let's draft short postmortem tomorrow. For now, I'm adding a one-liner to release-notes/internal: "Mitigated latency regression in eu-west after targeted kernel-selector rollback; improved experiment sync." :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Note: change window 03:45-04:15 UTC recorded. No customer-facing incidents opened.

maya: thanks team — closing loop for nightshift.

samir: closing the thread, will follow up with runbook PR in the morning.
